title: Evaluation of the incidence and predictors of compartment syndrome after recanalization of arterial occiusions in the lower extrem ity
summary:
If blood flow is restored in occluded vessels of the lower extremity, swelling of the extremity may occur. At its maximum severity, compartment syndrome occurs. Acute compartment syndrome is a condition in which increased pressure within a closed fascial space reduces capillary blood flow below a level necessary for tissue viability.
If the pressure is not relieved quickly, soft tissue demise and peripheral nerve damage can occur.
The treatment of choice is immediate surgical repair of the affected compartments to achieve normalization of tissue pressure.
conditions: Atherosclerosis of the peripheral arteries: pelvic-leg type, with exertion-induced ischemic pain, walking distance of less than 200 meters

interventions.name: Patients with arterial recanalizations of the lower extremity performed at the University Heart Center Freiburg-Bad Krozingen (location Bad Krozingen)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with arterial recanalizations of the lower extremity (femoro-popliteal artery or bypass) performed at the University Heart Center Freiburg-Bad Krozingen (location Bad Krozingen)
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients treated for lower extremity stenosis
- Patients who received interventional treatment due to stenosis of the upper extremity or in the venous flow area
